description: Supported static TypeScript contracts for the WASI 0.3 production compiler

tiers.name: Tier 1: Web Standard Primaries
tiers.description: Universal web and ECMAScript primitives available without environment-specific imports

tiers.name: Tier 2: Node Core Builtins
tiers.description: Node.js platform primitives mapped to WASI 0.3 host capabilities

tiers.name: Non-Goals
tiers.description: Features explicitly excluded from AOT WebAssembly compilation

capabilities.name: Bounded P3 HTTP GET
capabilities.domain: Production compiler: perry:http buffered GET
invariants: Explicit scheme, authority, path/query, string-valued headers, and integer response byte limit are checked before network I/O
Responses preserve status, duplicate headers, exact header bytes, and body bytes; non-2xx status remains a response
Body EOF is followed by separate producer/request completion; native resources close before return
Response metadata, body views, and header views survive helper returns and collection
The independent http_json fixture checks status, one supported Content-Type, a 64 KiB cap, strict UTF-8, and JSON syntax
Resolved WIT worlds importing wasi:http/client@0.3.0 use standard canonical bindings with typed results and recoverable errors
differences: Tasks may overlap in resolved WIT components and must finish before the owning invocation returns
HttpResponse is guest-internal; component wrappers export status, text, or bytes
Numeric failures: 8 overflow, 12 invalid metadata/limit/index, 100 plus WASI HTTP error discriminant, 200 plus header error discriminant
Traps and interrupted calls require store disposal

capabilities.name: Bounded P3 HTTP Handler
capabilities.domain: Rust compile_http_handler API exporting wasi:http/handler@0.3.0
invariants: Typed request/response records preserve method, optional coordinates, duplicate header bytes, and bounded body bytes
Typed guest tasks and combinators can use P3 capabilities; invocations are serialized through body transfer and separate consumer completion
Responses are published before transmission; abandonment and consumer errors release streams, futures, resources, and invocation storage
Repeated calls are tested under a 1 MiB guest memory cap using independent Wasmtime P3 bindings
differences: Explicit request/response byte caps; status 200–599, with empty bodies for 204/205/304
Overflow returns the corresponding WASI body-size error; invalid response metadata and request producer failures return internal-error
Source exceptions and interrupted calls require store disposal; hosts must drive the P3 event loop through completion
Request trailers are consumed but not exposed; source Web Streams, response trailers, and cooperative cancellation are unsupported

capabilities.name: Native P3 Filesystem Metadata and Directories
capabilities.domain: stat, mkdir, unlink, rmdir, readdir from node:fs/promises; synchronous spellings and existsSync from node:fs
invariants: Shared normalized longest-prefix preopens confine paths and symlinks; mutation cannot remove preopen roots
Stats preserve unsigned file sizes, signed modification milliseconds, type predicates, and identity
Directory listings materialize UTF-8 names, omit dot entries, and await the separate producer completion after EOF
Options and argument effects precede validation and I/O; known duplicate fields use the last value
Stats, string arrays, and suspended directory buffers survive helper calls, collection, and retained Promise outcomes
Normal and recoverable-error paths release descriptors, entry streams, and completion futures
The corresponding node:fs/promises operations use the same wasi:filesystem/types@0.3.0 and wasi:filesystem/preopens@0.3.0 bindings with retained task outcomes
differences: Reusable plain option objects retain aliases, typed mutation, optional undefined fields, and field effects; stat supports bigint false and throwIfNoEntry true, and readdir supports UTF-8 encoding, recursive false, and withFileTypes false
mkdirSync, unlinkSync, and rmdirSync only accept omitted or undefined options
Directory order is host-defined, materialization uses memory proportional to contents, and absent modification timestamps return zero
Component Stats use the exported stats record and stats-kind enum; string arrays use list<string>, also inside numeric-error Result returns
Errors use one-based WASI 0.3 ordinals; existsSync returns false on filesystem errors, while host traps and cancellation require store disposal

capabilities.name: Native P3 Filesystem Reads
capabilities.domain: readFile from node:fs/promises and readFileSync from node:fs with omitted, literal, or runtime string encoding
invariants: Binary reads preserve arbitrary bytes and return independent mutable views
Text reads preserve BOMs, NULs, and valid UTF-8 with scalar string semantics
The shared transfer loop handles partial input and closure; successful EOF still awaits producer completion
Invalid options fail before I/O; read-only preopens work without requesting write permissions
Pending buffers and returned values survive collection; resources close on success and recoverable errors
Materialization uses storage proportional to file size, with multi-megabyte and repeated bounded-memory fixtures
String-or-byte kinds survive aliases, assignments, control flow, retained Promise outcomes, and component parameters/results
The corresponding node:fs/promises operations use the same wasi:filesystem/types@0.3.0 and wasi:filesystem/preopens@0.3.0 bindings with retained task outcomes
differences: Runtime string encodings return string-or-byte values; methods, indexing, and type-specific arguments require typeof narrowing
Component unions use the exported text-or-bytes variant with text(string) and bytes(list<u8>) cases
Plain option objects support encoding and the default or r flag, preserve current fields through helpers and mutation, and return a string-or-byte union when reused
Malformed text throws filesystem error 9 instead of Node replacement decoding
The binary encoding label returns Uint8Array, preserving the existing compiler contract; Node returns Latin-1 text for that label
Host traps and cancellation require store disposal

capabilities.name: Native P3 Filesystem Writes
capabilities.domain: Overwrite-only writeFile from node:fs/promises and writeFileSync from node:fs
invariants: Named aliases, namespace imports, and default imports retain binding identity; unused imports add no filesystem capability
String data preserves exact UTF-8 and NUL bytes; Uint8Array data writes only its visible range
Arguments and plain object fields execute in source order; aliases, typed mutation, optional undefined fields, and duplicate-field effects survive validation and collection
Invalid encodings, flags, and unknown option properties fail before opening or truncating a file
Normalized paths select the longest matching preopen on a component boundary; symlink resolution remains host-confined
Shared native stream writes preserve partial transfers and await an independent filesystem completion
Descriptors, writable ends, and completion futures close on normal and recoverable-error paths; suspended buffers survive sibling collection
The corresponding node:fs/promises operations use the same wasi:filesystem/types@0.3.0 and wasi:filesystem/preopens@0.3.0 bindings with retained task outcomes
differences: Options accept encoding strings, null, undefined, and reusable plain objects; runtime delete, getters, setters, methods, spreads, computed literal keys, and custom prototypes are diagnosed
Only the default or w flag is supported; UTF8 labels accept ASCII case, and binary encoding is restricted to byte data
Errors throw the one-based WASI 0.3 filesystem error ordinal; already written bytes are not rolled back
Host traps and cancellation require store disposal; plain objects remain guest-internal with nonrecursive structural types or simple interfaces

capabilities.name: Native P3 Output
capabilities.domain: Production compiler: perry:stdio byte writes and single-string console logging
invariants: writeStdout and writeStderr preserve arbitrary bytes and visible Uint8Array ranges
Shared native writes retry partial transfers and respect host backpressure
Successful transfer still awaits the separate capability completion future
console.log routes to stdout; console.error and console.warn route to stderr, preserving UTF-8 and embedded NULs and appending a newline
Output buffers remain traced while suspended, including collection by sibling tasks
Normal and recoverable error paths close writable ends and consume and drop completion futures
differences: Byte writes are owned tasks; console calls return void but may suspend for host output
Console supports exactly one string; formatting and other argument forms are diagnosed
Output errors throw numeric codes: 1 I/O, 2 invalid byte sequence, 3 broken pipe; already written bytes remain visible
Host traps and cancellation require store disposal; returned streams and callbacks need further ownership support

capabilities.name: Scalar UTF-8 Text
capabilities.domain: Production compiler: UTF-8 text operations and component string boundaries
invariants: Length, indexing, slicing, search positions, and string iteration count Unicode scalars
String for-of evaluates its input once and retains that snapshot across mutation and P3 waits
Nested loops preserve update effects and route break/continue through crossed finally clauses
Unicode case conversions, code-point construction, split, and join preserve valid UTF-8
Literal regex search uses immutable compiled tables, returns reusable scalar positions, and allocates no guest storage
Canonical boundaries retain byte lengths; completed serial calls reclaim their invocation storage
differences: Unpaired surrogate escapes and UTF-16 code-unit APIs are diagnosed
Custom iterator protocols and labeled loop exits are unsupported; JSON is described separately in compiler.p3_json
Regex support is literal string.search with u/s flags; constructors, stored regex values, other flags, lookaround, backreferences, and property escapes are diagnosed
Implicit string coercions are restricted; traced loop collection reclaims dead temporaries, while returned-stream and callback owners remain incomplete

capabilities.name: Stored P3 Promise Outcomes
capabilities.domain: Production compiler: typed guest tasks, async WIT imports, native operations, and repeated await
invariants: A source task starts eagerly and its caller continues while native P3 work is pending
Aliases preserve Promise identity and repeated awaits retain statically typed success values and numeric rejection
Native P3 threads settle one shared outcome and notify registered observers once
A FIFO reaction queue preserves registration order, eager execution to first suspension, and return-promise adoption after finally
Promise records and reference-bearing outcomes share the guest heap, survive collection, and are reclaimed after result copying
Guest rejection enters catch and finally at await; host traps remain outside the language error channel
differences: Stored Promises require the host's component async stackful and threading features
Promise parameters are guest-internal; constructors and callback reactions remain unsupported
Detached call statements are diagnosed; unresolved work at return traps. Public calls execute serially; entries that bypass host serialization trap on the invocation guard
Traps and interrupted calls require store disposal. Cooperative cancellation and returned stream ownership are not yet exposed

capabilities.name: Typed P3 Clock and Random Calls
capabilities.domain: performance.now, Date.now, Math.random, crypto.getRandomValues, crypto.randomUUID, and promise-based node:timers/promises.setTimeout
invariants: Clocks and randomness use typed shared lowering plans and WASI 0.3 canonical adapters
Named and namespace timer imports preserve binding identity; the perry:clocks and perry:random source facades remain available
Arguments execute once in source order, with clock durations converted from milliseconds to nanoseconds
Monotonic reads return fractional milliseconds and system-clock reads return signed whole epoch milliseconds
Random filling preserves byte-view identity and its visible range, validates type and the 65536-byte quota before host calls, skips empty views, and loops over P3 short reads
UUIDs use fresh random bytes with v4 version and variant bits; UUID text and filled views survive collection, retained Promises, suspension, and disposal
Clock and random imports contain only selected functions and share adapters when multiple operations use the same interface
Unused declarations add no component imports; all emitted function bodies retain their referenced dependencies
UTF-8 values, exceptions, and async invocation ownership remain shared across capabilities
Host failures trap independently of guest exception handlers
Timer promises map to wasi:clocks/monotonic-clock@0.3.0 wait-for; delays below 1, above 2147483647, or NaN become 1 ms, and fractional delays are truncated
differences: Only direct calls and literal namespace member names are supported; dynamic lookup, capability function values, and spread arguments are diagnosed
The timer subset accepts one numeric delay; value and AbortSignal options are unsupported. The lower-level waitFor facade traps on invalid or overflowing durations
Random destinations support Uint8Array only; invalid supported value kinds throw numeric 1 and oversized views throw 2, while other typed-array classes are diagnosed
Native random calls returning zero progress or too many bytes trap; prior writes are not rolled back
Date objects and process context are scoped separately in compiler.p3_dates and compiler.p3_context; context mutation and callback timers are deferred under D1/D5
Public calls execute serially; cooperative cancellation is not exposed and interrupted calls require store disposal

capabilities.name: P3 Immutable Date and Temporal Values
capabilities.domain: Production compiler: immutable UTC Date and typed Temporal.Instant / Temporal.PlainDateTime
invariants: Date.now() reads whole signed UTC epoch milliseconds from the P3 system clock
Construction requires a statically known number and preserves time clipping and invalid dates
Constructed dates have distinct object identity and aliases retain identity
getTime() returns the timestamp or NaN for invalid dates
ISO formatting covers the entire clipped range, including negative timestamps, year zero, and signed six-digit years
Invalid ISO serialization throws numeric 1 through shared catch/finally completion handling
Dates and ISO strings survive helpers, object properties, retained Promises, suspension, and repeated allocating loops under a 64 KiB guest cap
Pure epoch/ISO computations require no WASI imports
differences: Date values are guest-internal; component boundaries carry UTC ISO strings
Omitted, copy, nonnumeric, and multi-argument constructors, calendar getters, valueOf, setters, string parsing, dynamic methods, and method arguments are diagnosed
Invalid ISO errors are numeric rather than Error objects

Temporal supports ISO string factories, Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds/epochMilliseconds, PlainDateTime fields/add({days}), and toString(); bracket annotations, options, additional calendars/zones, and implicit JSON serialization are unsupported

capabilities.name: P3 JSON and Shared Guest Graphs
capabilities.domain: Production compiler: strict UTF-8 JSON parsing and compact serialization through the component boundary
invariants: Parsed objects and mixed arrays preserve primitive tags, identity, nested mutation, and retained values across helpers, collection, and native suspension
Serialization preserves ECMAScript number formatting, duplicate-key replacement and property ordering; undefined fields are omitted and undefined array elements or holes become null
Undefined root serialization returns undefined; Dates produce ISO strings or null when invalid
Numeric error codes 1, 2, and 3 report syntax, unpaired surrogate escapes, and depth/cycles through catch/finally and declared WIT errors
Checked Rust codec adapters borrow disjoint guest storage outside measured helper data/stack; allocating loops and repeated large inputs reclaim temporary graphs
Pure JSON source tasks require no WASI imports; selected text helpers and P3 capabilities share the same guest memory
differences: Strings count Unicode scalars and reject unpaired surrogate escapes
Object keys must be strings; runtime delete, sparse arrays, and heterogeneous mutation are diagnosed. JSON value-tree reads preserve primitive tags.
Revivers, replacers, indentation, custom prototypes, sparse array literals, general array methods and extra array properties are unsupported
Unsupported byte-view, Stats, decoder, and Promise serialization throws numeric 12; errors are numbers rather than Error objects

capabilities.name: P3 Process Context
capabilities.domain: Production compiler: read-only process.env, process.argv, and process.cwd()
invariants: Only selected wasi:cli/environment@0.3.0 functions are imported and read lazily once per instance
Cached argument-array identity and valid UTF-8 values survive component returns, helper calls, retained Promises, collection, and native suspension
Retained heap roots preserve instance-local snapshots while invocation temporaries remain reclaimable
Environment and arguments are read-only; assignment, deletion, mutating methods, and bulk writes are diagnosed through aliases, casts, containers, and helper calls
Environment-only tasks do not link JSON formatting or coercion helpers
Object.keys and string-valued Object.values produce independent snapshots in insertion order; duplicate native environment keys replace values without moving their keys
JSON snapshots preserve cached environment values and parsed copies are independent
Host failures trap without running guest finally; store disposal releases pending native work
differences: Arguments use the host-provided list without synthetic Node executable/script prefixes
The initial directory defaults to / only when absent; an explicitly empty directory remains empty
Text operations count Unicode scalars
Missing environment keys return undefined; Object.values throws 12 for nonstring fields in ordinary objects
Numeric-looking dictionary keys keep insertion order; JavaScript integer-key sorting is deferred under D2
Object.assign accepts plain object targets/sources and ignores nullish sources; other primitive sources, prototypes, and spread arguments remain unsupported

capabilities.name: Guest Function Values
capabilities.domain: Calling synchronous guest function values with retained lexical captures
differences: Escaped callbacks and captures are deferred under D5.

capabilities.name: Timers
capabilities.domain: Direct setTimeout/setInterval and clearTimeout/clearInterval calls with synchronous guest callbacks and retained arguments
differences: Callback timers are deferred under D5; direct waits use native P3 clocks.

capabilities.name: Typed Promise Combinators
capabilities.domain: Promise.all, Promise.allSettled, and Promise.race over dense typed arrays and tuples
invariants: Operands are registered once; aggregate results preserve input order and retained identity
all rejects on the first observed rejection; allSettled retains status/value/reason records
race settles once and leaves losing operations owned until they complete
Finite heterogeneous tuple outcomes retain explicit static types
Empty all and allSettled settle to empty arrays; empty race remains pending and cannot escape its owning call
Shared observers register each operand once; joining does not sequentially await operands or rebuild pending lists on wake
differences: Requires a resolved WIT world and the pinned host threading features
Arbitrary iterables and thenables are unsupported; rejection payloads are numeric
Cooperative cancellation and returned stream ownership are not yet exposed

capabilities.name: global.fetch
capabilities.domain: Fetch mapped to wasi:http/client@0.3.0
differences: Not implemented; R6/R7 require standard fetch, cancellation, and Web Streams. The bounded perry:http GET operation is available.

capabilities.name: process.exit
capabilities.domain: Global process.exit with an omitted, literal undefined, or numeric safe-integer code
invariants: Maps directly to wasi:cli/exit@0.3.0#exit-with-code with an eight-bit status
Immediately terminates CLI scripts and named component exports without running subsequent statements or finally blocks
Validates numeric codes before invoking the host; a returning exit host traps
differences: process.exitCode and guest RangeError objects for invalid numeric codes remain required restoration work
Nonnumeric values and extra arguments are rejected at compile time; invalid runtime numeric values currently trap

capabilities.name: Uint8Array Byte Views
capabilities.domain: Byte construction, indexed access, and shared subviews used by randomness and filesystem APIs
invariants: Numeric lengths create zero-filled views; array/view inputs copy the visible bytes
Construction and indexed writes apply wrapping byte conversion; invalid indices do not alias valid elements
Subarrays share storage and resolve negative bounds relative to the current view
Byte views survive object properties, helper calls, retained Promise outcomes, and collection
Canonical list<u8> parameters and results preserve arbitrary bytes and copy visible subview ranges before reclamation
differences: Other typed-array classes, ArrayBuffer interoperability, Node Buffer compatibility, and broader Uint8Array methods are outside the tested subset
JSON serialization of byte views throws numeric 12; callers must choose an explicit text or numeric-array representation

capabilities.name: Dynamic Code Evaluation (eval / new Function)
capabilities.domain: Runtime evaluation of dynamic JavaScript strings
differences: Runtime code generation is outside the static TypeScript contract.

capabilities.name: Child Process Spawning
capabilities.domain: Spawning arbitrary OS processes via fork / exec
differences: Arbitrary host process spawning is outside the supported capability contract.
